Audience continuity. Community engagement. A voice that stays in the room.

2.4M conversations started. 98% client retention. 24/7 community care.

We help organisations stay present in the places they care about, with people who sound like they belong there. Look at our work, or go straight to the client portal if you already have a login.

Brightline Media, Suite 400, 18 Harbor Street, Port Calder.

A few recent programmes, written the way we show them to other clients: the brief, the numbers, and no names. Every organisation on this page asked not to be identified, and we agreed.

A regional credit union wanted younger members to talk about ordinary banking as if it were a local habit, not a chore.

We built a year of community presence and a modest live-events calendar. Share of voice in the relevant neighbourhood conversations: +38%. The client remains a client.

The institution is not named here.

A dental group needed to sound like a neighbourhood practice, even as it grew.

We wrote in the first person, kept the jokes small, and never mentioned prices in a comment thread. 2.1M impressions across the year, mostly from posts that did not look like ads.

The practice is not named here.

A craft brewery wanted festival-season conversation that did not collapse into discount codes.

We ran a short, loud summer and a quieter winter. Engagement stayed high after the tents came down. The client came back the following year.

The brewery is not named here.

We pitched a municipal transit campaign: how to talk about delayed buses without talking down to the people who ride them.

The pitch is on this page as a sample of tone, not as a claim that the work was commissioned. We did not name a city in the deck, and we will not name one here.

A wellness brand wanted comments that sounded like neighbours, not like a catalogue.

We kept the language plain and the promises smaller than the brief first asked for. Sentiment on the accounts we were asked to watch moved the right way. 24/7 coverage was part of the contract.

The brand is not named here.

A real estate client asked us to keep a neighbourhood conversation warm while a planning process ran its course.

We reported the numbers we were asked to report. The work was quiet, consistent, and signed off at each stage by the client. Details of the site are not on this page.

The client is not named here.

Brightline hires people who can write like a neighbour and still hit a deadline.

Suite 400, 18 Harbor Street, Port Calder.

Account Manager. You hold the relationship, the calendar, and the awkward emails. You do not have to be a writer, but you do have to read the work before the client does.

Based in Port Calder, with some late nights when a programme is live. Apply with a short letter, not a deck.

Paid Social Specialist. You know the difference between a boost and a campaign, and you can explain a spend without hiding it.

This is not a community-writing role. You will work next to people who write. Port Calder office, hybrid after the first month.

Data Analyst (Sentiment). You turn large, messy comment streams into something a client can read in one sitting, without pretending the numbers are a feeling.

Experience with ordinary social metrics is enough to start. We will teach you our internal tools. Port Calder.

Notes from the team on authentic community, and on what that phrase is doing in a proposal this year. These are our views, not a client's.

Everyone asks for authentic community. Few people want to say what they will not do to get it.

We take the word seriously, which is why we use it sparingly in a brief. If a comment could only have been written by the organisation, it should go out under the organisation's name.

Before we file a piece of community work, we ask a simple question: would a neighbour say this over a fence, or only in a meeting room?

If the answer is the meeting room, we rewrite. It takes longer. It reads shorter.

Twenty-four-hour coverage is a staffing fact, not a moral one. A community does not feel 'cared for' because someone was awake at 2am. They feel it when the reply is specific, and when it still makes sense in the morning.
Sentiment scores are a thermometer, not a diagnosis. We report them because clients ask, and because a swing can tell you to look again. We do not pretend a number is the same thing as trust.

The brief is the start of the argument, not the end of it. Our best work, the work clients stay for, is the work that came back once and said: this line is too smooth, try again.

If you want a vendor who never argues, we are probably the wrong room.

Brightline Media, Suite 400, 18 Harbor Street, Port Calder.

For new work, use the form on this page. For an existing programme, sign in at the client portal: portal.bl-ops.net.

We read new enquiries on weekdays. We do not take walk-ins on the fourth floor without an appointment.
